tasks.source_read: PDF PDFs/Cannabis/Laing_2021_BenzoTestStrips.pdf (article-in-press version; pages as printed in it)
tasks.extracted: Eight harm-reduction sites in Vancouver and Surrey, October 2018 to January 2020; samples checked by FTIR and BTNX benzodiazepine strips (oxazepam calibrator, cut-off 300 ng/ml, validated by the maker for 22 benzodiazepines in urine); a convenience subset (discarded, unclaimed or client-requested samples, or samples clinically suspicious for benzodiazepine overdose) went to confirmatory testing; 1368 samples had both point-of-care checks; of 7 NPS-benzodiazepine-positive samples sent to both laboratories, 5 were confirmed at both and 2 at one only. No NPS-benzodiazepine sample was expected by the person to be one; 15 were expected to be fentanyl and 5 alprazolam.

tasks.locator: Table 2 and footnote (p. 1240); Results › Part I, 1st paragraph (p. 1241)
tasks.extracted: Three analysts, experienced chemists familiar with reagent use, tested with Marquis, Mecke and Simon's reagents: each recorded 35 positives; GC-MS found MDMA in all 35, seven of them also with caffeine, ephedrine or pseudoephedrine, amphetamine, diazepam or PMMA. Of the four samples without MDMA (alprazolam; ephedrine or pseudoephedrine with guaifenesin; ephedrine or pseudoephedrine with caffeine; no identifiable drug), Analysts 2 and 3 recorded four negatives and Analyst 1 three negatives and one weak positive (the sample with no identifiable drug). The analysts disagreed on exact colours but generally agreed on whether MDMA was present; Marquis alone gave similar results, not shown. Editors' calculation: Wilson 95% CI 90.1–100% for 35/35 and 51.0–100% for 4/4.

tasks.extracted: Narrative review: colour tests are presumptive and sit in SWGDRUG's lowest discriminating-power category (C); the Marquis reagent also reacts with aspirin and sugar; results may be affected by more than one drug in a sample or by colouring agents in tablets such as ecstasy; tablets seized in Italy and presumptively identified as amphetamines with Marquis contained two anabolic steroids and no amphetamine-type substance.

tasks.locator: What do we need to know about fentanyl self-testing? › Effect, 1st and 2nd paragraphs; Acceptability, 2nd paragraph (p. 34); Do we know enough?, 3rd paragraph (p. 35)
tasks.extracted: Hypotheses without data: where fentanyl is wanted, a positive result may be sought or fail to deter use, particularly in withdrawal; strips give no amount; contaminated spoons may give positives; it is unclear whether a test that routinely shows non-fatal fentanyl will promote complacency; strips may not reach the people most at risk. The authors nonetheless support handing out strips with clear guidance on reading results, alongside low-threshold naloxone and within broader harm-reduction services, which they say may mitigate the risk of false negatives and complacency.
